requirements.requirement: /tmp on node1 mounted with noexec, nosuid, and nodev enforced
requirements.summary: Baseline showed /tmp was part of root ext4 with no restrictions (cmd-857be2e3619b44d6). Executor added a tmpfs fstab entry and mounted /tmp live with rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime (cmd-800ae76a4d4244b2), then functionally verified script execution was denied (rc=126), a setuid bit was ignored at execution, and a device node write was denied (same command). After a reboot (boot_id changed from e5ad1dea... to 7cb7bd3a..., cmd-f10790bc6f0d443f and cmd-fc3e57a2d3a44c64), post-reboot checks (cmd-05aa45224d56429a) confirmed fstab entry persisted, findmnt showed the same tmpfs options active, and all three functional tests (exec, setuid, device node) again failed as expected.

requirements.requirement: /dev/shm on node1 mounted with noexec, nosuid, and nodev enforced
requirements.summary: Baseline /dev/shm was already tmpfs with nosuid,nodev,noexec by default (cmd-857be2e3619b44d6), but executor still added an explicit fstab entry to guarantee persistence and remounted it (cmd-800ae76a4d4244b2), then ran the same exec/setuid/device functional checks confirming enforcement. Post-reboot (cmd-05aa45224d56429a), fstab entry persisted and findmnt showed two stacked tmpfs mounts on /dev/shm (the default boot-time 'shm' mount plus the fstab-driven mount), both carrying the required noexec,nosuid,nodev options; functional exec test on /dev/shm was denied (rc=126) confirming enforcement survived reboot.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — noexec/nosuid/nodev enforcement on /tmp and /dev/shm, surviving reboot — are directly satisfied. The executor captured a full evidence chain: pre-change baseline, fstab and live-mount changes, functional enforcement tests, a genuine reboot confirmed by boot_id change, and post-reboot re-verification of both fstab persistence and functional enforcement on both mount points. Test artifacts were cleaned up and the reboot was performed safely without data loss.
limitations: The provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol overlaps with and is satisfied by the same reboot the task itself required, so no additional restart evidence was needed or missing.

The double-stacked tmpfs mount on /dev/shm post-reboot (visible in findmnt output) is a minor implementation quirk rather than a functional gap, since both stacked mounts carry the required restrictive options.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor actions were tightly scoped to the task: fstab backup before edit (cmd-800ae76a4d4244b2, retained as a timestamped .bak file — low-risk, standard safety practice, not cleaned up but harmless residue), functional test artifacts (exectest.sh, busybox_suid, nulltest device node) created in both pre- and post-reboot verification passes and explicitly removed via 'sudo -n rm -f' at the end of each run (cmd-800ae76a4d4244b2, cmd-05aa45224d56429a) — bounded and fully reverted. The reboot itself was a necessary, task-relevant disruption to prove persistence, correctly backgrounded to allow the session to survive disconnection. The 12 failed polling commands (cmd-14d61594dc1e4349 through cmd-6a5b9d0040404c2f) are expected connection-reset/timeout noise while the node was down mid-reboot, not state-changing mutations. One minor inefficiency: mounting /dev/shm via fstab caused a stacked double tmpfs mount rather than a clean single remount, but this is a benign side effect of Alpine's default shm mount plus the new fstab entry, not a harmful or insecure residue.
